long_biography.plain_text:
Bill Joy's reputation was established before Sun Microsystems. As a graduate student at Berkeley, he helped create and distribute BSD Unix and wrote tools including vi and the C shell. He then joined three other founders in building Sun in 1982, serving as chief scientist and shaping technologies including Solaris, SPARC and Java before leaving in 2003.

Investment became Joy's main occupation after Sun. He spent nine years at Kleiner Perkins backing early-stage energy and materials technologies, then joined Water Street Capital as principal and chief scientist. This makes Finance & Investments his current industry, while his original wealth-creation story remains Sun's technology business. Sun's market value, revenue and eventual acquisition price were corporate figures, not measures of his personal fortune.
